clue.text: What must be done to let out airport shop?

parts.note: a duty is what one is obliged to do
to free someone is to release them

explanation.surface: A puzzled traveller wonders what it takes to be allowed out of the airport shopping area.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops past airport security sell goods without excise or import tax, hence the name.

clue.text: Steep stair finally tackled by theatrical dame

indicators.note: something tackled is grabbed and held, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Dame Judi Dench is a renowned stage and screen actress

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An elderly actress bravely takes on a steep staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective about the stair, but it is the verb meaning to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep something is to soak it thoroughly in liquid, which is to drench it.

clue.text: Janitor carelessly loses one determined fellow

indicators.note: done carelessly, things end up jumbled out of order
something lost is no longer there, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A sloppy caretaker misplaces a hard-working colleague.
explanation.definitionFit: To work like a Trojan is to labour with great effort, so a Trojan is a resolute, tireless person.

clue.text: Bush's history altered in note

indicators.note: placed in another piece, the rearranged letters sit inside it

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A US president's record is rewritten in a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the president, but the 's is 'is' and the bush is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a shrub with bright yellow flowers in early spring.

clue.text: Aid for photographer harassing supremo in SW city

indicators.note: placed in another piece, the jumbled letters sit inside it

parts.note: Exeter is the county city of Devon in south-west England

indicators.note: harassing someone leaves them flustered and disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A paparazzo helper hounds a top boss somewhere in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter is a cathedral city in Devon, in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposure meter measures light so a photographer can set the correct aperture and shutter speed.

clue.text: Colourless Brighton & Hove players with final twist …

indicators.note: a twist at the end means only the closing pair of letters gets turned round

parts.note: Brighton & Hove Albion is an English football club

explanation.surface: A football team plays dully until a late turnaround, the sentence trailing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Brighton & Hove Albion is a football club on England's south coast; swap its last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An albino lacks pigment, so as an adjective in looser use it stands for a creature lacking colour.

clue.text: Tipped amateur coming in fast

indicators.note: something coming in enters another piece and sits within it

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
A is the abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: A racing tipster backs an amateur jockey arriving quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed but is the religious fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipped and leant both mean tilted or inclined to one side, past tense.

clue.text: Mess about, losing first soldier in battle

indicators.note: losing the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to tinker is to fiddle or mess about
a man is a private soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier fooling around in combat gets knocked out first.
explanation.walkthrough: Inkerman was an 1854 battle of the Crimean War.
explanation.definitionFit: Inkerman is the name of a Crimean War battle fought by British and French against Russia.

clue.text: Exaggerates, as rutting stags fight?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: carries something too far

definitions.note: a phrase, read as two words OVER DOES
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: male deer battle for female deer

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words: stags in the rutting season fight over the female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo is to take something beyond what is proper; the second reading is a playful split into a preposition plus female deer.

clue.text: … got pier replaced as morale-booster

indicators.note: things replaced are put back in a different arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing the Brighton theme, the town gets its pier rebuilt to cheer everyone up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done chiefly to flatter one's self-esteem, so it boosts morale.

clue.text: Loud squawk obscures last of sinister rustling

indicators.note: to obscure something is to cover it up, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a cackle is a loud harsh cry, as of a hen

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A noisy bird's call drowns out some faint, menacing rustle.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackle is a series of small sharp sounds, close to the dry noise of rustling leaves or paper.

clue.text: Racing driver aims for this standard after fluctuating

indicators.note: coming after means the first-named piece goes second in the final order

parts.note: a chequered history is one of mixed fortunes
a standard is a flag or banner

explanation.surface: A racer's performance level is erratic.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white flag is waved as the winner crosses the line, so every motor racer drives toward it.

clue.text: Mad keen touring Arizona

indicators.note: someone touring a place travels all round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: to keen is to wail in grief, to cry
AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona

explanation.surface: Someone is wildly enthusiastic about a trip round Arizona.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad keen' reads as one phrase meaning very eager; split it, and keen is the verb for lamenting.
explanation.definitionFit: Crazy and mad are everyday synonyms for insane or wildly foolish.

clue.text: Shady wife replacing husband felt hot and faint

indicators.note: one item replacing another means swapping a letter for a different one

parts.note: a shady spot is sheltered from the sun
W is the abbreviation for wife
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife takes her husband's place in the shade while he swelters.
explanation.definitionFit: To swelter is to be uncomfortably oppressed by heat, enough to feel weak.

clue.text: Complete price for crossing street

parts.note: thorough means complete, utter
a fare is the price of a journey

explanation.surface: Someone is quoted an all-in charge for getting across the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughfare is a road open at both ends, a public street that runs through for passage.

clue.text: Golfer's best reason for scrapping old socks?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: sinking the ball with the tee shot
second meaning: a sock worn through gets thrown away

explanation.definitionFit: An ace in golf is a single-stroke score on a hole; literally, a worn sock has a gap in it.

clue.text: Press review mentioned more weird standards

parts.note: a crit is an informal word for a critique or review

indicators.note: something mentioned is spoken, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

parts.note: eerier means more weird

explanation.surface: A newspaper critique talks about yardsticks becoming stranger.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the benchmarks or tests by which things are judged.

clue.text: Handcuffed fanatic, one leaving under escort

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a maniac is an obsessive enthusiast
I is the Roman numeral for one
someone led is escorted

explanation.surface: A cuffed extremist is taken away under guard, one of the group leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Manacles are shackles for the wrists, so manacled means restrained as with handcuffs.

clue.text: Men in service breed butterflies

parts.note: to rear animals is to breed them
the red admiral and white admiral are butterflies

explanation.surface: Some men in the forces have a hobby of raising butterflies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' here means the armed services, specifically the Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear admirals are senior officers in the Navy, one of the armed services.

clue.text: Celebrated brief liaison between France and Sweden

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so its final letter goes
between places this piece in the middle of the two others

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
an amour is a love affair
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: A short-lived romance between a French and a Swedish celebrity makes the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated and famous are synonyms for widely known and acclaimed.

clue.text: Break in continuity hit USA badly …

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pause in operations struck America hard, the sentence running into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiatus is a gap or pause in a sequence that is otherwise continuous.

clue.text: Stripped of underwear, cross-dresser died (passed over)

indicators.note: being stripped of something means having it taken away

parts.note: a transvestite dresses in clothes of the opposite sex
a vest is a British undershirt
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A grim tabloid line: a cross-dresser was stripped and died, the bracket a euphemism for death.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt, so it counts as underwear. '(passed over)' looks like a euphemism for dying but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To transit is to pass across or over something, as a planet crossing the face of the sun.

clue.text: … it beat underworld boss

parts.note: 'it' is old slang for sex appeal, SA
to tan someone's hide is to beat them

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, something defeated a gangland chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' suggests a crime lord; here it is the ruler of hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan, the Devil, rules hell, which is the underworld of the dead.

clue.text: National leaders of Irish Republic are quite implacable …

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letters are taken

parts.note: the first letters of the five words

explanation.surface: A statement that Irish republicans are stubborn, the sentence running on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A national is a citizen of a country; an Iraqi is a citizen of Iraq.

clue.text: … one tells Queen to come back in a while

indicators.note: coming back means going the opposite way, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina
later means after a while

explanation.surface: Someone informs the monarch that she should return shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: A relater is a person who relates, that is who tells or narrates a story.

clue.text: Sentry's view dismissed

parts.note: a look is a view
a batter dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A guard's opinion has been rejected out of hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout is a person posted to watch for danger, the job of a sentry.

clue.text: Retreat in craft that's burning

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it

parts.note: art is a craft or skill
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: A boat used as a hideaway has caught fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a boat, which fits the burning scene, but it means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate, and its Latin root and older sense is literally burning or glowing.

clue.text: Goes on striking first two fearsome women

indicators.note: striking out the first two means crossing off the opening pair of letters

parts.note: to progress is to go on, advance

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on hitting the first two scary women in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a monstrous or frighteningly cruel woman.
